Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — useful overview for the infra and search team. Per our call, we want to confirm the trial scope and lock down the access plan so we can start the technical work on Monday. High-level asks from our side:

- Short POC period (3 weeks): verify inference latency on 100k request/day pattern, embedding quality for search rerank, and cost estimates for dedicated capacity if we scale.
- Credentials for API (server-to-server keys) + service account SSO invite for our eng lead (Ayesha).
- IP allowlist ranges for our egress and any static endpoints your side exposes.
- A mutual checklist of success criteria (latency P95 <= 220ms on our baseline, embedding NDCG > 0.72 on our sample queries).

Can you confirm what you need from us to provision API keys and SSO invites? Also, who at Redwood will own the onboarding tasks so we can assign internal stakeholders?

Thanks,
Daniel

Hi Daniel — great to continue this thread. Appreciate the clear list. Below is a proposed starter plan and the minimal artifacts we need from CloudCrest to begin provisioning and getting the trial running:

Proposed POC timeline (3-week sprint):
- Week 0 (kickoff, days 1–2): finalize success criteria, exchange credentials list, SSO invites & IP allowlist, share sample dataset (anonymized).
- Week 1 (days 3–9): Redwood provides sandbox API keys, connector guide, and a short runbook. CloudCrest runs smoke tests and validation queries.
- Week 2 (days 10–16): scale tests to 100k req/day pattern; embedding eval and rerank benchmarks; collect latency/cost telemetry.
- Week 3 (days 17–21): joint review, cost projection for Dedicated capacity, and decision window.

Minimum items we need from you (please provide by Friday COB PST to hit the Monday kickoff):
1) List of SSO invite emails + roles (example: ayesha.malik@cloudcrest.com — eng-lead).
2) Static IP ranges for allowlist (or confirmation you prefer token-based and we’ll share endpoints).
3) Sample query set (CSV) and ~2k sample documents for embedding quality checks (anonymized).
4) Which environments should we target (sandbox only or sandbox + staging)?

Redwood owners and responsibilities:
- Marissa (me) — overall POC owner, outcomes/governance, escalation point for timeline blockers.
- Karthik Iyer — technical lead for credentialing, IP allowlist, API key issuance, and validation.
- Camila Reyes — success criteria and embedding evaluation; will run NDCG and qualitative checks.
- Jonas Weber — ops/contact for logging, telemetry, and quota policies.

Access mechanics (what we’ll provide):
- Short-lived server API keys for sandbox (recommended flow) + instructions for rotating keys.
- SSO invites (SAML/SCIM) if you want Redwood console access for teammates — request emails and role mapping required.
- IP allowlist endpoints: we will publish a short list of egress IPs and any static collector endpoints; if you prefer an IP-range CIDR we can provide that by EOD Friday.

Attachments I’m sharing now: 1) redwood-trial-connector-instructions.pdf (quick start), 2) cloudcrest-prelim-sla.xlsx (sample SLA/uptime assumptions). Drive link below has the runbook and template success-criteria doc.

If this plan looks good I’ll have Karthik kick off the key provisioning and Camila schedule the evaluation checkpoints with your team.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
